evidence.note: Built the skeleton and immediately ran both an individual family json (i32) and the full aggregate runner to establish a baseline pass rate before implementing.
After implementing numeric ops, ran per-family jsons (i32, block, f32) and grepped FAIL lines to localize failures — the core per-family verification loop.

Used block.json FAIL analysis to identify missing Call/CallIndirect, patched them (36-37), rebuilt, re-ran a batch of family files (38) and re-ran block.json grepping FAIL to confirm (39-40) — a genuine fix-and-reverify loop.
Ran the aggregate runner and computed MVP-only rates (89.9%), but diagnosis was categorical (counting assert_invalid/return/trap) rather than drilling into individual semantic FAIL reasons.
Abandoned before any SIMD implementation; the per-family SIMD verification loop — the bulk of the task surface — was never exercised.

reasoning: The agent demonstrated a real implement→run-family-json→read-FAIL→fix→re-run loop for MVP families plus periodic aggregate monitoring, matching anchor 5 and reaching slightly toward 8. However, its failure diagnosis stayed at the category-counting level rather than drilling into specific semantic edge cases (anchor 10), and it never verified any SIMD family because it abandoned the task, so the verification behavior was neither deep nor sustained across the full horizon.
